children: Nifty 500 companies broadly delivered a "sharp and broad-based acceleration in revenue growth", "volatile margins" and "strong earnings growth yoy" in Q1FY27, excluding oil and gas, Kotak Institutional Equities said in a latest note on Monday.

"Topline trends were broadly similar across market caps, even as PAT growth was higher for smaller companies." However, consensus earnings upgrades were selective, suggesting a "calibrated outlook of the Street at present".

Nifty 500 companies saw 20% sales growth, 5% EBITDA growth and 10% PAT growth in Q1FY27. The broader universe delivered 20% year-on-year revenue growth, or 15% excluding energy. EBITDA grew 5% year-on-year, or 19% excluding energy, while PAT grew 10%, or 20% excluding energy.

Kotak noted that "revenue growth has seen acceleration across most sectors", with 18 of 31 sectors delivering more than 15% revenue growth. This resulted in a "broadening of EBITDA and PAT growth in 1QFY27".

Sales growth across market capitalisations "drove strong profit growth". The contribution of the top 100 companies to Nifty 500 revenues increased modestly to 66%, while their contribution to PAT remained largely stable at 72%.

"Sales growth (ex-oil & gas) was between 13% and 17% across market caps, with sequential acceleration seen in large-caps and small-caps." However, mid- and small-cap companies "outpaced large-caps in EBITDA and PAT growth in 1QFY27".

Margins remained volatile in aggregate. Nifty 500 companies reported a 181-basis-point sequential and 253-basis-point year-on-year decline in margins in Q1FY27, excluding BFSI. Excluding oil and gas and BFSI, margins expanded 153 basis points sequentially and 10 basis points year-on-year.

Kotak said "strong yoy margin expansion was seen in commodity/energy-linked sectors" such as building products, electric utilities, gas utilities, metals and mining, real estate and specialty chemicals. "Large yoy margin contraction was seen mostly in automobiles & components, capital goods, consumer staples, healthcare services, oil & gas and transportation."
The brokerage noted that "RM costs (ex-oil & gas) remain at elevated levels", while "employee expenses/sales were broadly stable ex-oil & gas".

Looking ahead, consensus expects "stable and broad-based earnings growth over FY2027-28E". Consensus is currently projecting 13% and 18% earnings growth on a full-float basis for Nifty 500 companies over FY2027E and FY2028E, respectively.

"Earnings expectations remain relatively broad-based", with 15 of 31 sectors currently projected to deliver more than 20% earnings growth in FY2027E. However, earnings estimates are "broadly unchanged on aggregate", even as select sectors witnessed noticeable changes in estimates.

title: Nifty 500 companies see broad-based revenue acceleration in Q1FY27; margins volatile: Kotak
